proposed_fixes.title: FancyZones Win+Arrow movement loses focus when focus-follows-mouse is enabled
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Moving the focused window under a stationary pointer may activate another window when Windows focus-follows-mouse is enabled, so later Win+Arrow input targets the newly activated window.
plan: Trace focus and pointer position while FancyZones handles Win+Left/Right under Windows focus-follows-mouse.
Keep the moved window active or move the pointer consistently with the snap operation.
Add a regression test for repeated Win+Arrow movement while another window lies under the pointer.
verification: With focus-follows-mouse enabled and Override Windows Snap active, repeat Win+Left/Right and verify the originally focused window continues moving.

confidence.rationale: FancyZones movement likely interacts with Windows focus-follows-mouse when the moved window uncovers another window; current-build behavior is unknown.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming the issue affected all windows on Windows 10 22H2 and v0.85.1. Could you confirm whether it still reproduces on your current PowerToys/Windows versions with “Activate a window by hovering” and Override Windows Snap enabled? If you can, note whether placing the pointer over the moved window prevents the next Win+Arrow from switching targets. This distinguishes focus activation from FancyZones snap selection.
